quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When should you yield your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Yield whenever it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when driving behind a large vehicle so you can:

options.text: See around the sides of the vehicle.
Stop other drivers from pulling behind the large vehicle before passing.
Avoid the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: See around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles pulling trailers block the driver's view. Increase your following distance so you can see around the sides and see the road ahead.

questions.question: When driving through curves, the most important thing is to:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle may be hard to control in curves because of inertia. Slow down before entering a curve to maintain control.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines separate:

options.text: No-passing zones.
Lanes moving in the same direction.
Lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn the steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want it to go. Once the vehicle starts to straighten, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: It is legal to go faster than the speed limit when passing another vehicle.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot exceed the speed limit, even when passing another vehicle.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that wet pavement will be slippery and they should reduce speed.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, glance:

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, turn into:

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: When turning, move from your lane into the first available legal lane. When turning from a two-way to a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Overcorrect.
Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Release the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You can no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You do not have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the direction the arrow pointed. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red traffic light after stopping?

options.text: When you are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.
When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you can turn left at a red light only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs that prohibit this turn.

questions.question: What does a solid white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up in a traffic lane or on the shoulder. Continue driving to the next exit or crossroad. Other drivers do not expect vehicles backing up and collisions are likely.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: What are signs called that require drivers to follow an instruction?

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking the rules on these signs can result in a fine.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Road work or maintenance is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work or maintenance is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs warn about construction, maintenance, and utility work areas. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe. Fines for traffic violations may be doubled in these areas.

questions.question: If another car is passing you in a no-passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and stay in your lane.
Slow down to let the other car safely get back in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let the other car safely get back in your lane.
questions.explanation: Help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely and easily. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow traffic light ahead and have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves right and then left.
The road ahead curves left and then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right and then left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings and alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road that has not washed away yet. Be extra careful when driving during the first 30 minutes of rain.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Prepare to stop, if needed.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop, if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill. A vehicle may be stalled just out of sight. Slow down before going over a hill so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: If heavy smoke is covering the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Reduce your speed, move as far to the right as possible, and stop off the roadway.
Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed, move as far to the right as possible, and stop off the roadway.
questions.explanation: Slow down right away. Drive to the right side of the road and stop off the roadway. Check if it is safe to continue. Heavy smoke can hurt your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: If a car is following you too closely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, change lanes if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the other driver to pass you.

questions.question: When passing a car that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Assume that the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: Expect that a parked car's door may open as you pass. Be careful when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: You and another driver reach a four-way stop at the same time. The driver is on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: There are oncoming cars on your left and parked cars on your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer down the middle between oncoming traffic and parked cars.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC.

questions.question: If your car's rear is skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
questions.explanation: If you skid on wet or icy roads, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, brake firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit sign show?

options.text: Only a recommended driving speed.
The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe driving speed under all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit shows the highest legal speed for that road under good conditions. You may need to drive slower in bad weather or poor road conditions.

questions.question: For a driver age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 or older cannot legally drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Drunk driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out of your vehicle and check behind it before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are near. This is the safest way to back out of a driveway.

questions.question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move into a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. If you can, move to another lane to create space for them. If you cannot move lanes, adjust your speed so incoming vehicles can enter traffic safely.

questions.question: When should you start slowing down as you exit the interstate?

options.text: Halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your interstate speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then immediately slow down to the posted exit ramp speed.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers entering your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes or pass in an intersection. Before changing lanes, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder and watch for other drivers trying to enter your lane.
